articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document represents the May 1992 issue, Volume 3, Number 5, of the "SJAA EPHEMERIS." It is identified as the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association, suggesting it contains news, updates, and other information pertinent to the club and its members.

articles.title: Directions to Houge Park Site of SJAA Public Star Party
articles.summary: This document provides detailed directions to Houge Park for San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) public star parties and other events, including specific instructions for parking and telescope access. It also features an extensive calendar of SJAA activities for May and June, encompassing star parties, general meetings with guest speakers on astrophotography and cosmology, astronomy classes, an auction, and notes on upcoming celestial events like lunar and solar eclipses. The editor includes apologies for previous directional errors and promotes organizational news.

articles.title: Star Parties by ed
articles.summary: This article details two recent star parties at Fremont Peak and Grant Ranch, both significantly impacted by dense fog, cold temperatures, and strong winds. Despite the adverse conditions, some observations were made, including Jupiter and Comet Tanaka-Machholtz, and a technical experiment to sharpen a homemade telescope's image with a mask proved effective. The author emphasizes the challenging weather experienced at both locations.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: The article reports on recent comet activity, noting a new discovery expected to be visible soon. It details the status of Comet Shoemaker-Levy, with the 1991d designation fading and 1991a brightening, while Comet Mueller is believed to have disintegrated after perihelion.

articles.title: Periodic Comet Howell (1992c):
articles.summary: Periodic Comet Howell (1992c) was successfully recovered by S. Larson and J. Scotti from Kitt Peak on March 5, observed at magnitude 21. It is anticipated to brighten considerably, reaching magnitude 15 by early next year.

articles.title: Comet Tanaka-Machholz (1992d):
articles.summary: Amateur astronomer Don Machholz independently discovered Comet Tanaka-Machholz (1992d) on March 31, 1992, confirming an earlier sighting by Z. Tanaka. The comet, initially misidentified regarding its speed, will make its closest approach to the sun on April 22 at 1.26 AU and become an evening sky object by mid-June. Machholz also shares personal news of his son's birth and a new job offer during the discovery week.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for two comets: Shoemaker-Levy (1991a₁) and Tanaka-Machholz (1992d). For each comet, it lists observational data including date, celestial coordinates (RA and DEC), elongation, sky visibility, and apparent magnitude over several weeks. A separate, brief section lists attendees, possibly for an observing event or meeting focused on constellations near Leo.

articles.title: TIME AGAIN FOR THE GREAT SJAA AUCTION
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is holding its annual auction on May 2nd at Houge Park, commencing at 2:00 PM. Attendees are encouraged to bring items for sale, including 'white elephants,' and funds for making purchases. Further details can be obtained by contacting the SJAA hotline, Jim Van Nuland, or any Board of Directors member.

articles.title: Flashing Telrad
articles.summary: This document describes a circuit modification for a Telrad finder scope, enabling it to be used more effectively with very faint astronomical objects. The modification involves a 6 to 9 Volts switched power supply to enhance its performance for low-light viewing.

articles.title: NOTES:
articles.summary: This document provides technical notes regarding a TELRAD device, highlighting the polarity sensitivity of its LED illuminator and instructing to mark wires before disconnection. It also advises removing a now-unnecessary 50Ω resistor from the TELRAD switch/control. Additionally, it lists the Radio Shack part number for a TLC555 device (276-1718), noting that total parts cost should be under $5.00.

articles.title: SJAA OBSERVATORY STRUCTURE DESIGN TEAM REPORT
articles.summary: A design team has been formed to plan the structure for the SJAA observatory at the proposed Grant Ranch site. The team has met twice, discussing observatory priorities and reviewing the site's physical layout. Key design considerations include public service as the primary purpose, accommodating large groups (20-40 people), handicap access, simple expansion, low maintenance, and fitting a park environment, all for a 10-11" Schmidt-Cass telescope.

articles.title: RAISIN BREAD
articles.summary: Bob Madden expresses concern about low attendance at general meetings, emphasizing the value of past talks by Ethan Clifton, Dr. Schramm (clarifying the Big Bang with raisin bread), and Bill Dellinges. He highlights impressive upcoming presentations by John Gleason on astrophotography and Dr. Romani on Neutron Stars, Black Holes, and Cosmology, urging members to show interest and support.

articles.title: SJAA Public Star Party Site
articles.summary: The document identifies the location for the SJAA Public Star Parties, specifically Houge Park. It includes a map detailing the park's position relative to several major streets and Highway 17, indicating it is a designated public viewing site.

articles.title: SJAA AUCTION ASTRONOMICAL ITEMS MIRRORS - LENSES - EYE-PIECES - MOUNTS - AND COMPLETE TELESCOPES
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting an auction for astronomical items. Members are encouraged to bring their surplus mirrors, lenses, eyepieces, mounts, and complete telescopes to sell, and also to purchase new equipment. Ten percent of all sales will be donated to the SJAA.

articles.title: Lunar/Phases Date Rise Tran Set
articles.summary: This document presents a concise almanac detailing the lunar phases for the month of May. It lists the exact time and date for the New Moon, First Quarter, Full Moon, and Last Quarter, alongside their respective rise, transit, and set times. This information provides essential data for tracking lunar cycles and planning observations.

articles.title: Nearer Planets
articles.summary: This document presents astronomical data for the 'nearer planets' (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn) for three specific dates in May. For each planet, it details their rise, transit, and set times, distance in Astronomical Units (AU), and apparent magnitude.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V Mag - 26.72
articles.summary: This document, titled "SOL Star Type G2V Mag - 26.72" referring to our Sun, presents a structured list of astronomical data. Each entry includes celestial coordinates, a date (DD-MM format), and three numerical values, likely representing specific observation times or event times related to the Sun or objects observed in relation to it.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document lists Julian Dates and corresponding calendar dates in May, alongside pairs of times. These times likely represent the start of morning astronomical twilight and the end of evening astronomical twilight, defining the period each day when astronomical darkness is not present. The data illustrates the progression of twilight and daylight durations over the month of May.

articles.title: Siderial Time
articles.summary: This document provides a set of sidereal time values corresponding to specific astronomical events and dates in May, observed at 0000 PDT. It lists sidereal times for 'Transit Right' on May 7th, 'Ascention' on May 17th, and 'Local Midnight' on May 27th. The data appears to be a schedule or log of celestial timing.

articles.title: Darkest Saturday Night May 02
articles.summary: The article announces a "Darkest Saturday Night" event for May 02, providing key astronomical times in Pacific Daylight Time: sunset at 19:58, twilight ending at 21:41, and moonrise at 20:16. It also includes an administrative update noting that membership dues will increase to $12 on July 1st, the first such increase in 10 years.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This article, titled "ASTRO ADS," is a classifieds section offering free advertising for noncommercial sellers of astronomically related products and services. Submissions are due by the 12th of each month and run for approximately three months. The document lists various used astronomical equipment for sale, including telescopes, eyepieces, mounts, and astrophotography gear, with seller contact information.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing various membership options including 'Membership only', 'Membership / S&T', and 'Junior', along with their respective fees. It provides instructions for submission to the Treasurer, Jack Peterson, including contact addresses and a telephone number. The form also mentions the SJAA's monthly publication, "EPHEMERIS", and provides guidelines for article submissions.
